newsitem.title: ERITREA: Rebels say capture state ministers in south Sudan.
newsitem.headline: Rebels say capture state ministers in south Sudan.

text.p: A Sudanese rebel spokesman said on Friday the rebels captured several state ministers and members of the Buheirat state parliament when they captured the state capital Rumbek in southern Sudan in April.

"The forces of the SPLA captured a number of officials of the Khartoum government in Lakes (Buheirat) State at its capital Rumbek", Yassir Arman of the rebel Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) told Reuters in Asmara.

"Among them there are ministers, officials of the state, senior members of its parliament, and also directors of ministries, and a medical doctor who works for the Sudanese army medical unit. We also captured a radio broadcasting station in a good condition," he said.
The spokesman said the medical doctor had resumed his work as a physician in the rebel-controlled areas of Sudan. "It is on his own demand," said Arman.
He said the rebel radio, The Voice of Sudan, had conducted interviews with the prisoners, including the medical doctor.

The spokesman said the prisoners included Police Lieutenant Colonel Sabino Mulwal, who was the minister of engineering affairs in Buheirat State, Colonel Majok Deng, who was the speaker of the Buheirat state parliament, and Andrea Uodo Maktab, secretary general of the State Council.

"Until now, the NIF government never admitted the falling of Rumbek town to the hands of the SPLA," the spokesman said. "By capturing Rumbek the SPLA is now in the heart of Bahr al-Gazal, and it is a big blow to the agreement between the NIF (the National Islamic Front) and Riek Machar", he said.
Riek Machar, a defector from the SPLA, is the leader of the small southern factions which signed a peace agreement with the Islamist government in Khartoum last month.
